content: Hmm...Maybe simplify it a bit, but that's just me I guess

Goal - Step 2
* Consider removing the word "non-alphabetical". The meaning seems clear without it, and the current wording may accidentally imply that English letters themselves are non-alphabetical characters, with digits or underscores being *other* non-alphabetical characters.

Goal - Step 3
* Consider changing "some consecutive number of zeros" to simply "consecutive zeros".

Goal - Reason 1
* Consider replacing "may not" with "must not" for clarity.

* Please replace "the multiplication symbol" with "an asterisk".

* The current description doesn't seem to cover all possible repeat-block syntax that appears in the cases:

  (a) "marked by some variable/number": "Variable Lineup" test includes "|ALL|", but "|ALL|" is neither a variable (as it contains "|") nor a number.

  (b) The statement also doesn't mention that arbitrary spaces or newlines may appear between the components of a repeat block.

* Can empty repeat blocks occur?

* Can nested repeat blocks occur?

* The semicolon-removal rules are currently ambiguous:

  (a) A repeat block is said to "begin" with a variable or number, so "repeat blocks may not begin with semi-colons" could be interpreted as disallowing ";[variable]" rather than disallowing "{;". If the intended meaning is that no semi-colon may appear immediately after {, that should be stated explicitly.
  
  (b) Similarly, "repeat blocks may not end with semi-colons" could be interpreted as disallowing "};". If the intended meaning is that no semi-colon may appear immediately before }, that should also be stated explicitly.

Goal - Reason 2
* "there may be other variables with the same shortened name that got overridden": What "other" refers to is unclear here. Consider rewriting it as:
  
  some variables may share the same shortened name and become overridden.

Constraints / Cases
* Consider removing the constraint "The standard notation of a number will never have the same length as the original number." and instead including such cases. I explained the rationale in my comment on the clash version of the puzzle.

* What should happen if there are consecutive newline characters (i.e. blank lines)? Should every newline still be replaced with a semi-colon? If blank lines cannot appear in the input, please add a constraint stating so explicitly.

Cases
* I'll review these after the above issues have been addressed.

Thanks.

* It feels unclear exactly when variable duplication should be resolved. A user might misunderstand that they should resolve duplicates the moment they encounter them while scanning the code. If one follows this logic, in the "Variable Lineup (Validator)" case, they might assign "b" to "abigail" the moment they find it, because at that point, they don't yet know that "ben" appears later. Consider explaining that the process consists of a reservation phase and a resolution phase.

* The definition of a repeat block states "A repeat block is marked by some variable/number, followed by the multiplication symbol (*), ...". However, in the "Indentation" case, "(RepeatY+x)" is being accepted as a repeat block. Conventionally, "(RepeatY+x)" would be classified as an expression, which is a different concept from a variable or number.

* The cases "Condensed Code" and "Condensed Code (Validator)" violate the constraint "The given CGL code will not contain any semi-colons (;).".

* The author's solution produces a repeat block that begins and ends with semi-colons for the following case.

Input:

```
7
Loop * {

someVar = Loop + 1
::<< someVar
Loop += Loop + someVar

}
```

Output from the author's solution:

```
L*{;s=L+1;::<<s;L+=L+s;}
```

Thank you.

Based on my previous Clash of Code contribution, which was deemed too difficult. https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/1463709636a102fd7f1963357e1b82b5ae05b5

More test cases to come!
Thanks @kozuechan! I am also aware of some of these inconsistencies after trying to craft more test cases myself. Will definitely be fixing them before marking this puzzle as ready.
